title: The moon split
hookLine: the Hour draws near and the moon is split (54:1)

lines: THE END OF TIME, AND A MOON.
cards: A clear night at Mina, just outside Mecca. The moon over the mountains. A group of men from Quraysh have come to the Prophet ﷺ with a challenge: show us a sign.
What happened next is reported by several Companions, in the most trusted hadith collections, and it gave the fifty-fourth surah its name: Al-Qamar, the Moon.
Its first verse holds two things that don't obviously belong together: the end of time, and a moon.

teach.b: Pickthall: "The hour drew nigh and the moon was rent in twain." Iqtarabat as-sa'ah: the Hour has come near. Wanshaqqa al-qamar: and the moon split.
In Sahih al-Bukhari, 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud says he was there. The moon split in two, one part over the mountain and one beyond it, and the Prophet said: bear witness.
Anas ibn Malik reports that the Meccans had asked for a sign, and they were shown this.

teach.h: MOST SAY: AN EVENT IN HIS LIFETIME.
teach.b: Most classical scholars read the verse this way, as an event in the Prophet's lifetime. A minority read the past tense as a vivid way of describing something certain to come with the Hour.

teach.h: THEY SAW A SIGN AND CALLED IT MAGIC.
teach.b: Verse two gives the reaction: if they see a sign, they turn away and say, a magic that keeps going. The surah's point isn't astronomy.
It's the gap between seeing and accepting: people asked for a sign, saw one, and found a word to explain it away. Why put the moon next to the Hour?
Commentators note that the Hour's nearness runs through these late surahs. The Prophet once held up two fingers side by side and said: I and the Hour were sent like these two.

The split moon is presented as an early crack in the ordinary, a sign the world's order isn't permanent. One honest note. You may see claims online that space agencies photographed proof of the split.
No such confirmation exists, and the tradition never rested on one. It rests on the reports of people who said they saw it.

how: Muslims recite Surah Al-Qamar and count the splitting of the moon among the Prophet's miracles; the Prophet recited it, with Surah Qaf, in the Eid prayers, and many imams still do.

games.q: you're one of the Meccans who asked for a sign. you see the moon split. what does 54:2 say people like you did?
o: turned away and called it magic.
games.why: the surah's point is the gap between seeing and accepting.

practice: Find the moon tonight, whatever its phase, or picture the last one you remember. Look long enough for it to stop being familiar: a stone hanging in nothing, lit by a sun you can't see. If you pray, you can say subhanallah.

wordCard.voice: Al-Qamar, the Moon, the surah named for the night the moon split in two before men who asked for a sign. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: the hour draws near. The moon is still up there, a reminder that time moves. Day six hundred one, done.
